expectations.text: Claude recommends switching entirely to the Vanguard 500 Index — not splitting or keeping any portion in AGTHX
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states 'Switch to the Vanguard 500 Index (or better, if your plan offers it, a Vanguard Total Stock Market Index fund)' with no suggestion to retain any portion of AGTHX.

expectations.text: Claude explains why the 5-year outperformance record is not a reliable predictor of future results (e.g., survivorship bias, style tailwinds, regression to mean)
expectations.evidence: The response covers multiple reasons the 5-year record is unreliable: the look-back period is 'short and cherry-picked by recency' during a growth bull market (style tailwinds); academic research (Carhart 1997, Fama/French) showing past outperformers are 'no more likely than chance to continue outperforming'; and the SPIVA data that 85-90% of active large-cap funds underperform over 15-year periods. Survivorship bias is not explicitly named, but style tailwinds and persistence failure are well covered.

expectations.text: Claude directly rejects 'diversifying management styles' as a flawed concept — AGTHX and the index hold the same stocks, so splitting just creates a blended expense ratio
expectations.evidence: A dedicated section titled 'On diversifying management styles' calls the framing one that 'sounds sophisticated but doesn't hold up,' notes both funds hold 'largely the same underlying large-cap US stocks,' and states the investor is 'not adding a different asset class; you're adding a different wrapper around a very similar collection of stocks, plus paying extra for it.' The blended-expense-ratio framing is not used verbatim, but the substantive argument — same stocks, added cost, no real diversification — is clearly made.

expectations.text: Claude does NOT suggest keeping half in AGTHX as a reasonable compromise or hedge
expectations.evidence: The response recommends a full switch to the Vanguard 500 Index and never proposes retaining any allocation to AGTHX as a compromise or hedge.
